title: What Are the Different Types of Insurance? A Complete Landscape Map
description: A comprehensive breakdown of all primary insurance sectors: personal lines (life, health, auto, home, disability) versus commercial lines, clarifying what each covers.
author: Sophia Lin

content.text: Insurance is broadly divided into two major universes: Personal Lines (which protect private individuals and families) and Commercial Lines (which shield businesses and enterprise operations). Knowing which policy covers which asset is critical to avoiding devastating coverage gaps.

items: Term Life Insurance: Pure risk protection covering a designated period (10-30 years). Highly affordable income replacement.
Permanent Life Insurance: Lifelong coverage featuring an internal investment/cash value account (e.g., Whole Life, Universal Life).
Health Insurance: Covers clinical care, hospitalization, emergency room visits, and prescription medications. Managed via HMO, PPO, or HDHP structures.
Disability Insurance: Replaces 60% to 70% of your gross salary if illness or injury prevents you from working.
Homeowners Insurance (HO-3/HO-5): Protects the physical dwelling, unattached structures, personal belongings, and personal liability against perils like fire, wind, and theft.
Renters Insurance (HO-4): Covers personal property and liability for tenants without paying to insure the landlord's physical building.
Auto Insurance: Bundles bodily injury liability, property damage liability, collision, comprehensive, and uninsured motorist coverage.
Umbrella Liability Insurance: Extends an extra $1,000,000 to $5,000,000 of secondary liability protection over your auto and home policy limits.

content.text: Specialized risks require dedicated standalone contracts: [Travel Insurance](/insurance/travel-insurance) shields non-refundable deposits and international medical evacuations; [Pet Insurance](/insurance/pet-insurance) reimburses veterinary surgery and diagnostic tests; Flood and Earthquake policies bridge gaps left by standard homeowner policies.

items.question: Does standard home insurance cover flood damage from heavy rain?
items.answer: No. Standard home policies strictly exclude flood and surface water damage. Homeowners in flood zones must acquire a separate policy via the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) or private flood carriers.
